title: Machine groups through the ZPA API, SDKs and Terraform
aliases: can I create a machine group with terraform

prose.text: This subject covers machine groups in the API, the SDKs and Terraform.

checks.do: Whether the task needs to create or change a group, which no documented client does; use the console.
Which certificate key a client reads from a machine record.
Whether a Python caller needs the machines list, which its model does not carry.
Whether the caller is in a custom microtenant, where groups are read-only.

api-read-only.statement: ZPA's API documentation describes machine group resources as read-only. The documented operations are a GET on the collection and a GET on a single group.

quotes: Machine group API resources allow you to read machine groups.

summary-endpoint.statement: The Go and Python SDKs also call `GET /machineGroup/summary`, a name-and-ID listing; the OpenAPI capture does not list that path.

sdk-no-writes.statement: The Go machinegroup package exposes Get, GetByName, GetAll and GetMachineGroupSummary, and the Python MachineGroupsAPI exposes list_machine_groups, list_machine_group_summary and get_group. Neither SDK has a create, update or delete function for machine groups.
sdk-no-writes.conditions: Rests on absence: both files were read in full and define no other public function.

terraform-data-source-only.statement: The ZPA Terraform provider has a `zpa_machine_group` data source and no machine group resource.
terraform-data-source-only.conditions: Rests on absence: searched the provider's docs/resources and zpa/ directories (2026-10-18) and found data_source_zpa_machine_group.go but no resource file or resource document for machine groups.

quotes: Use the **zpa_machine_group** data source to get information about a machine group created in the Zscaler Private Access cloud.

data-source-attributes.statement: The data source exports `id`, `creation_time`, `description`, `enabled`, `modified_by`, `modified_name`, `microtenant_id`, `microtenant_name` and a `machines` list. Each machine entry has `fingerprint`, `issued_cert_id`, `machine_group_id`, `machine_group_name`, `machine_token_id` and `signing_cert`.

data-source-feeds-policy.statement: The provider documents the machine group data source as the way to reference a machine group in an access, timeout, forwarding, inspection or isolation policy.

quotes: This data source can then be referenced in an Access Policy, Timeout policy, Forwarding Policy, Inspection Policy or Isolation Policy.

name-lookup.statement: The Go SDK's GetByName lists machine groups with the name as a search filter and returns the first result whose name matches case-insensitively.

search-note.statement: The provider asks that search queries for the machine group data source avoid multiple spaces and special characters.

quotes: To ensure consistent search results across data sources, please avoid using multiple spaces or special characters in your search queries.

paging.statement: The machine group list takes `page` and `pagesize`, with a default page size of 20 and a maximum of 500.

quotes: If not provided, the default page size is 20. The maximum page size is 500.

python-model-omits-machines.statement: The Python MachineGroup model reads `id`, `name`, `enabled`, `description`, `creationTime`, `modifiedTime` and `modifiedBy`. It has no attribute for the `machines` list or the microtenant fields.
python-model-omits-machines.conditions: Rests on absence: the model's __init__ and request_format were read in full and mention no machines or microtenant key.

quotes: self.creation_time = config["creationTime"] if config and "creationTime" in config else None
self.modified_by = config["modifiedBy"] if config and "modifiedBy" in config else None

microtenant-permissions.statement: Under microtenant configuration permissions, machine groups are fully editable in the default microtenant and read-only in a custom microtenant, while machine provisioning keys are not visible in a custom microtenant.

quotes: | Machine Provisioning Keys | Full | Not visible |

signing-cert-field-name.summary: The OpenAPI capture names the per-machine certificate `enrollmentCert`; the SDKs and Terraform call it `signingCert`.

positions.says: A machine record carries an `enrollmentCert` object.
The Go SDK reads and sends the certificate under `signingCert`.
The Terraform data source exports it as `signing_cert`.

signing-cert-field-name.impact: A client written from the OpenAPI capture and one written from the SDK read different keys for the same certificate, so a field that is empty in one may be populated in the other.

create-endpoint-absence.title: Whether the live API accepts a write on machine groups
create-endpoint-absence.detail: The documentation and OpenAPI capture show only GET operations and the SDKs and provider expose none. No source states that the live API would reject a POST, PUT or DELETE on /machineGroup. Try the write in a scratch tenant and compare with the console, which does add, edit and delete groups.
create-endpoint-absence.blocks: saying the API cannot create a group, as opposed to saying no documented client does
